issues.legal_issue: A finding on an heirship issue in an earlier suit between the same parties is res judicata in a later possession suit when the issue was directly and substantially in dispute and its determination was necessary to decide the earlier suit fully.
material_facts: In the earlier suit, the claimant sought a declaration of title and an injunction, relying both on an alleged oral will and on his lawful possession of the property.

The claimant disputed that the opposing parties were related to the deceased owner or had any title superior to his possessory claim; the opposing parties asserted that they were the deceased’s collaterals and heirs.
The relationship issue was pleaded, denied, framed as an issue, and tried with evidence.
The trial court found that the opposing parties had not proved the relationship, but the appellate court reversed that finding and held that they were collaterals of the deceased.
The later suit sought possession on the basis of the opposing parties’ title as heirs, and the same parties were involved.
issues.conclusion: The appellate finding that the opposing parties were the deceased’s collaterals was res judicata and barred the claimant from disputing their heirship in the later suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, including Explanation 3, a matter is directly and substantially in issue when it is raised by one party, denied by the other, and its decision would materially affect the suit. The question is assessed from the pleadings, issues, and decision. An issue may meet that test even if the suit was dismissed on another ground, where the issue was relevant to a claim based on possession and to whether the opposing parties had a superior title. The Court also held that the parties’ litigation was under the same title because the earlier claim included a right to remain in possession, not merely a claim under the alleged will.

rule.if: later_possession_suit and same_parties and prior_claim_included_possessory_right and relationship_disputed_in_prior_suit and relationship_issue_tried and prior_appellate_finding_on_relationship and relationship_material_to_relief

predicates.later_possession_suit: The later proceeding is a suit for possession in which a party relies on title derived from the deceased owner.
predicates.same_parties: The parties to the earlier suit and the later suit are the same.
predicates.prior_claim_included_possessory_right: In the earlier suit, the claimant relied on a right to remain in possession as well as on any separate asserted source of title.
predicates.relationship_disputed_in_prior_suit: In the earlier suit, one party asserted and the other denied that the opposing parties were related to the deceased owner and entitled to succeed to the property.
predicates.relationship_issue_tried: The relationship dispute was framed as an issue and the parties led evidence on it in the earlier suit.
predicates.prior_appellate_finding_on_relationship: An appellate court in the earlier proceeding made a finding determining the relationship dispute.
predicates.relationship_material_to_relief: Determining the relationship dispute was relevant to whether the opposing parties had a title superior to the claimant’s asserted possessory right and was needed to resolve the claims for relief.

issues.definition: When the same parties litigate a later possession suit, and a relationship issue was tried and decided on appeal in an earlier suit in which the claimant also relied on possession and the issue mattered to the relief sought, the earlier finding bars relitigation of that issue.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate determination of an issue is not open to collateral attack as a nullity merely because the appellate court may have erred in deciding whether an appeal from the relevant finding was competent.
material_facts: The trial court dismissed the earlier suit but made a finding against the parties claiming heirship.
Those parties appealed the adverse finding, and the appellate court reversed it.
A preliminary objection that the appeal was not maintainable was rejected, and a revision challenging that decision was dismissed; that order became final.
In the later proceeding, the claimant argued that the appellate court lacked jurisdiction to make the finding because an appeal lay only from a decree.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court had jurisdiction to decide the question of appealability, and even if its decision on that question was erroneous, its judgment was not a nullity and could not be collaterally attacked.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an appeal lies from a decree; however, an appellate court’s potentially erroneous construction of its jurisdiction does not make its judgment a nullity where the court had authority to decide the appealability question. Section 44 of the Indian Evidence Act did not permit the collateral attack advanced here. Further, under Order 41 Rule 22 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the opposing parties could have challenged the adverse finding in the claimant’s competent appeal to support the decree.

predicates.later_proceeding_challenges_prior_appell: A party in a later proceeding seeks to avoid the effect of a finding made by an appellate court in an earlier proceeding.
predicates.prior_appellate_court_decided_appealabil: The appellate court in the earlier proceeding considered whether it could hear the appeal.
predicates.appealability_objection_rejected: An objection that the appeal was not maintainable was rejected, and that decision was not successfully set aside.
predicates.challenge_is_collateral: The later challenge attacks the earlier appellate court’s authority indirectly rather than through a successful direct challenge to its judgment.

issues.definition: When a party later attacks an appellate finding collaterally after the appellate court considered and rejected an objection to its authority to hear the appeal, the finding is not treated as a nullity merely because the decision on appealability may have been wrong.
